missing_requirements.title: Idempotent Blacklist Insertion and Storage Hygiene
missing_requirements.description: Blacklist state insertions for refresh token JTIs must be idempotent to prevent race conditions during concurrent reset events or duplicate propagation deliveries, and must incorporate token-lifetime-bound Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration.
missing_requirements.provenance: Distributed Systems Data Integrity & Security Standards
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: If multiple concurrent password reset requests or redelivered synchronization events occur, non-idempotent insertions can cause distributed lock contention or state corruption. Step 2: Without automatic TTL expiration aligned with the token's remaining validity, the blacklist storage would grow unbounded, causing memory/storage exhaustion. Step 3: Therefore, enforcing idempotent writes and bounded TTL expiry preserves data integrity and prevents resource degradation across all clusters.

missing_requirements.title: Partition-Tolerant Fail-Closed Access Gate
missing_requirements.description: If a cluster loses connectivity to the cross-cluster revocation synchronization layer or blacklist store, authentication verification must enforce a fail-closed posture for refresh token validation to prevent revoked token reuse during network partitions.
missing_requirements.provenance: Zero Trust Security Architecture & Distributed Failure Modes
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: During a network partition, isolated clusters cannot verify if a refresh token has been blacklisted due to a recent password reset. Step 2: A fail-open approach would allow compromised, pre-reset refresh tokens to successfully authenticate users during outages, defeating the security guarantee of the password reset. Step 3: Therefore, a fail-closed authorization gate must block refresh token validation when revocation status cannot be definitively confirmed.

Domain: 'auth_identity'

- [REQ-EXPLICIT-002] Refresh Token Blacklisting Across Clusters (EXPLICIT): Blacklist active refresh tokens across all deployment clusters upon session invalidation triggered by password reset.
- [REQ-DERIVED-001] Distributed Token Revocation Propagation (DERIVED_JUSTIFIED): Revocation lists or states must synchronize or be queryable across all independent clusters with bounded propagation latency.
- [REQ-DERIVED-002] Token Identifier Uniqueness and Extraction (DERIVED_JUSTIFIED): Refresh tokens or their unique cryptographic identifiers (JTI) must be extractable and matched against the revocation blacklist during authentication verification.
- [REQ-UNKNOWN-001] Token Storage Mechanism and Protocol Standards (UNKNOWN): The specific data store (e.g., Redis cluster, SQL database) and token format standards (e.g., JWT, opaque tokens) are unstated.
- [REQ-UNKNOWN-002] Cross-Cluster Sync Latency and Consistency Model (UNKNOWN): The exact acceptable replication lag or consistency model (e.g., strong vs. eventual consistency) for multi-cluster sync is unstated.

Coverage Audit Directive:
- Analyze what critical domain invariants, edge cases, failure modes, data integrity rules, or concurrency controls are MISSING from the above list to fulfill the prompt completely.
- Synthesize ONLY the missing requirements with 3-step why-chains.
- Do NOT duplicate any requirement already in Pass 1.
